NKJV.1: Then they told David, saying, “Look, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah, and they are robbing the threshing floors.”
NKJV.2: Therefore David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go and attack these Philistines?” And the LORD said to David, “Go and attack the Philistines, and save Keilah.”
NKJV.3: But David’s men said to him, “Look, we are afraid here in Judah. How much more then if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
NKJV.4: Then David inquired of the LORD once again. And the LORD answered him and said, “Arise, go down to Keilah. For I will deliver the Philistines into your hand.”
NKJV.5: And David and his men went to Keilah and fought with the Philistines, struck them with a mighty blow, and took away their livestock. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
NKJV.6: Now it happened, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, that he went down with an ephod in his hand.
NKJV.7: And Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah. So Saul said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town that has gates and bars.”
NKJV.8: Then Saul called all the people together for war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
NKJV.9: When David knew that Saul plotted evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”
NKJV.10: Then David said, “O LORD God of Israel, Your servant has certainly heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah to destroy the city for my sake.
NKJV.11: Will the men of Keilah deliver me into his hand? Will Saul come down, as Your servant has heard? O LORD God of Israel, I pray, tell Your servant.” And the LORD said, “He will come down.”
NKJV.12: Then David said, “Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?” And the LORD said, “They will deliver you.”
NKJV.13: So David and his men, about six hundred, arose and departed from Keilah and went wherever they could go. Then it was told Saul that David had escaped from Keilah; so he halted the expedition.
NKJV.14: And David stayed in strongholds in the wilderness, and remained in the mountains in the Wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God did not deliver him into his hand.
NKJV.15: So David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. And David was in the Wilderness of Ziph in a forest.
NKJV.16: Then Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose and went to David in the woods and strengthened his hand in God.
NKJV.17: And he said to him, “Do not fear, for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you. You shall be king over Israel, and I shall be next to you. Even my father Saul knows that.”
NKJV.18: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD. And David stayed in the woods, and Jonathan went to his own house.
NKJV.19: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is David not hiding with us in strongholds in the woods, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon?
NKJV.20: Now therefore, O king, come down according to all the desire of your soul to come down; and our part shall be to deliver him into the king’s hand.”
NKJV.21: And Saul said, “Blessed are you of the LORD, for you have compassion on me.
NKJV.22: Please go and find out for sure, and see the place where his hideout is, and who has seen him there. For I am told he is very crafty.
NKJV.23: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hides; and come back to me with certainty, and I will go with you. And it shall be, if he is in the land, that I will search for him throughout all the clans of Judah.”
NKJV.24: So they arose and went to Ziph before Saul. But David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon, in the plain on the south of Jeshimon.
NKJV.25: When Saul and his men went to seek him, they told David. Therefore he went down to the rock, and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard that, he pursued David in the Wilderness of Maon.
NKJV.26: Then Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain. So David made haste to get away from Saul, for Saul and his men were encircling David and his men to take them.
NKJV.27: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and come, for the Philistines have invaded the land!”
NKJV.28: Therefore Saul returned from pursuing David, and went against the Philistines; so they called that place the Rock of Escape.
NKJV.29: Then David went up from there and dwelt in strongholds at En Gedi.

NASB.1: Then they told David, saying, 'Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and are plundering the threshing floors.'
NASB.2: So David inquired of the LORD, saying, 'Shall I go and attack these Philistines?' And the LORD said to David, 'Go and attack the Philistines and deliver Keilah.'
NASB.3: But David's men said to him, 'Behold, we are afraid here in Judah. How much more then if we go to Keilah against the ranks of the Philistines?'
NASB.4: Then David inquired of the LORD once more. And the LORD answered him and said, 'Arise, go down to Keilah, for I will give the Philistines into your hand.'
NASB.5: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought with the Philistines; and he led away their livestock and struck them with a great slaughter. Thus David delivered the inhabitants of Keilah.
NASB.6: Now it came about, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, [that] he came down [with] an ephod in his hand.
NASB.7: When it was told Saul that David had come to Keilah, Saul said, 'God has delivered him into my hand, for he shut himself in by entering a city with double gates and bars.'
NASB.8: So Saul summoned all the people for war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.
NASB.9: Now David knew that Saul was plotting evil against him; so he said to Abiathar the priest, 'Bring the ephod here.'
NASB.10: Then David said, 'O LORD God of Israel, Your servant has heard for certain that Saul is seeking to come to Keilah to destroy the city on my account.
NASB.11: 'Will the men of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down just as Your servant has heard? O LORD God of Israel, I pray, tell Your servant.' And the LORD said, 'He will come down.'
NASB.12: Then David said, 'Will the men of Keilah surrender me and my men into the hand of Saul?' And the LORD said, 'They will surrender you.'
NASB.13: Then David and his men, about six hundred, arose and departed from Keilah, and they went wherever they could go. When it was told Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, he gave up the pursuit.
NASB.14: David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him every day, but God did not deliver him into his hand.
NASB.15: Now David became aware that Saul had come out to seek his life while David was in the wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.
NASB.16: And Jonathan, Saul's son, arose and went to David at Horesh, and encouraged him in God.
NASB.17: Thus he said to him, 'Do not be afraid, because the hand of Saul my father will not find you, and you will be king over Israel and I will be next to you; and Saul my father knows that also.'
NASB.18: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD; and David stayed at Horesh while Jonathan went to his house.
NASB.19: Then Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, 'Is David not hiding with us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of Jeshimon?
NASB.20: 'Now then, O king, come down according to all the desire of your soul to do so; and our part [shall be] to surrender him into the king's hand.'
NASB.21: Saul said, 'May you be blessed of the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.
NASB.22: 'Go now, make more sure, and investigate and see his place where his haunt is, [and] who has seen him there; for I am told that he is very cunning.
NASB.23: 'So look, and learn about all the hiding places where he hides himself and return to me with certainty, and I will go with you; and if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.'
NASB.24: Then they arose and went to Ziph before Saul. Now David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of Jeshimon.
NASB.25: When Saul and his men went to seek [him], they told David, and he came down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard [it], he pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.
NASB.26: Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain; and David was hurrying to get away from Saul, for Saul and his men were surrounding David and his men to seize them.
NASB.27: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, 'Hurry and come, for the Philistines have made a raid on the land.'
NASB.28: So Saul returned from pursuing David and went to meet the Philistines; therefore they called that place the Rock of Escape.
NASB.29: David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of Engedi.

WEB.9: David knew that Saul was devising mischief against him; and he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”
WEB.10: Then David said, “O Yahweh, the God of Israel, your servant has surely heard that Saul seeks to come to Keilah, to destroy the city for my sake.
WEB.11: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? Yahweh, the God of Israel, I beg you, tell your servant.” Yahweh said, “He will come down.”
WEB.12: Then David said, “Will the men of Keilah deliver me and my men into the hand of Saul?” Yahweh said, “They will deliver you up.”
WEB.13: Then David and his men, who were about six hundred, arose and departed out of Keilah, and went wherever they could go. Saul was told that David was escaped from Keilah; and he gave up going there.
WEB.14: David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. Saul sought him every day, but God didn’t deliver him into his hand.
WEB.15: David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life. David was in the wilderness of Ziph in the wood.
WEB.16: Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose, and went to David into the woods, and strengthened his hand in God.
WEB.17: He said to him, “Don’t be afraid; for the hand of Saul my father won’t find you; and you will be king over Israel, and I will be next to you; and Saul my father knows that also.”
WEB.18: They both made a covenant before Yahweh. Then David stayed in the woods, and Jonathan went to his house.
WEB.19: Then the Ziphites came up to Saul to Gibeah, saying, “Doesn’t David hide himself with us in the strongholds in the woods, in the hill of Hachilah, which is on the south of the desert?
WEB.20: Now therefore, O king, come down. According to all the desire of your soul to come down; and our part will be to deliver him up into the king’s hand.”
WEB.21: Saul said, “You are blessed by Yahweh; for you have had compassion on me.
WEB.22: Please go make yet more sure, and know and see his place where his haunt is, and who has seen him there; for I have been told that he deals very crafty.
WEB.23: See therefore, and take knowledge of all the lurking places where he hides himself, and come again to me with certainty, and I will go with you. It shall happen, if he is in the land, that I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.”
WEB.24: They arose, and went to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah on the south of the desert.
WEB.25: Saul and his men went to seek him. When David was told, he went down to the rock, and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard that, he pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.
WEB.26: Saul went on this side of the mountain, and David and his men on that side of the mountain; and David hurried to get away for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men surrounded David and his men to take them.
WEB.27: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and come; for the Philistines have made a raid on the land!”
WEB.28: So Saul returned from pursuing David, and went against the Philistines. Therefore they called that place Sela Hammahlekoth.
WEB.29: David went up from there, and lived in the strongholds of En Gedi.

NLT.1: One day news came to David that the Philistines were at Keilah stealing grain from the threshing floors.
NLT.2: David asked the LORD, “Should I go and attack them?” “Yes, go and save Keilah,” the LORD told him.
NLT.3: But David’s men said, “We’re afraid even here in Judah. We certainly don’t want to go to Keilah to fight the whole Philistine army!”
NLT.4: So David asked the LORD again, and again the LORD replied, “Go down to Keilah, for I will help you conquer the Philistines.”
NLT.5: So David and his men went to Keilah. They slaughtered the Philistines and took all their livestock and rescued the people of Keilah.
NLT.6: Now when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he brought the ephod with him.
NLT.7: Saul soon learned that David was at Keilah. “Good!” he exclaimed. “We’ve got him now! God has handed him over to me, for he has trapped himself in a walled town!”
NLT.8: So Saul mobilized his entire army to march to Keilah and besiege David and his men.
NLT.9: But David learned of Saul’s plan and told Abiathar the priest to bring the ephod and ask the LORD what he should do.
NLT.10: Then David prayed, “O LORD, God of Israel, I have heard that Saul is planning to come and destroy Keilah because I am here.
NLT.11: Will the leaders of Keilah betray me to him? And will Saul actually come as I have heard? O LORD, God of Israel, please tell me.” And the LORD said, “He will come.”
NLT.12: Again David asked, “Will the leaders of Keilah betray me and my men to Saul?” And the LORD replied, “Yes, they will betray you.”
NLT.13: So David and his men — about 600 of them now — left Keilah and began roaming the countryside. Word soon reached Saul that David had escaped, so he didn’t go to Keilah after all.
NLT.14: David now stayed in the strongholds of the wilderness and in the hill country of Ziph. Saul hunted him day after day, but God didn’t let Saul find him.
NLT.15: One day near Horesh, David received the news that Saul was on the way to Ziph to search for him and kill him.
NLT.16: Jonathan went to find David and encouraged him to stay strong in his faith in God.
NLT.17: “Don’t be afraid,” Jonathan reassured him. “My father will never find you! You are going to be the king of Israel, and I will be next to you, as my father, Saul, is well aware.”
NLT.18: So the two of them renewed their solemn pact before the LORD. Then Jonathan returned home, while David stayed at Horesh.
NLT.19: But now the men of Ziph went to Saul in Gibeah and betrayed David to him. “We know where David is hiding,” they said. “He is in the strongholds of Horesh on the hill of Hakilah, which is in the southern part of Jeshimon.
NLT.20: Come down whenever you’re ready, O king, and we will catch him and hand him over to you!”
NLT.21: “The LORD bless you,” Saul said. “At last someone is concerned about me!
NLT.22: Go and check again to be sure of where he is staying and who has seen him there, for I know that he is very crafty.
NLT.23: Discover his hiding places, and come back when you are sure. Then I’ll go with you. And if he is in the area at all, I’ll track him down, even if I have to search every hiding place in Judah!”
NLT.24: So the men of Ziph returned home ahead of Saul. Meanwhile, David and his men had moved into the wilderness of Maon in the Arabah Valley south of Jeshimon.
NLT.25: When David heard that Saul and his men were searching for him, he went even farther into the wilderness to the great rock, and he remained there in the wilderness of Maon. But Saul kept after him in the wilderness.
NLT.26: Saul and David were now on opposite sides of a mountain. Just as Saul and his men began to close in on David and his men,
NLT.27: an urgent message reached Saul that the Philistines were raiding Israel again.
NLT.28: So Saul quit chasing David and returned to fight the Philistines. Ever since that time, the place where David was camped has been called the Rock of Escape.
NLT.29: David then went to live in the strongholds of En-gedi.

David Saves Keilah

MSG.1: It was reported to David that the Philistines were raiding Keilah and looting the grain.
MSG.2:
David went in prayer to God: "Should I go after these Philistines and teach them a lesson?"
God said, "Go. Attack the Philistines and save Keilah."
MSG.3: But David's men said, "We live in fear of our lives right here in Judah. How can you think of going to Keilah in the thick of the Philistines?"
MSG.4: So David went back to God in prayer. God said, "Get going. Head for Keilah. I'm placing the Philistines in your hands."
MSG.5: David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He scattered their cattle, beat them decisively, and saved the people of Keilah.
MSG.6: After Abiathar took refuge with David, he joined David in the raid on Keilah, bringing the Ephod with him.
MSG.7: Saul learned that David had gone to Keilah and thought immediately, "Good! God has handed him to me on a platter! He's in a walled city with locked gates, trapped!"
MSG.8: Saul mustered his troops for battle and set out for Keilah to lay siege to David and his men.
MSG.9: But David got wind of Saul's strategy to destroy him and said to Abiathar the priest, "Get the Ephod."
MSG.10: Then David prayed to God: "God of Israel, I've just heard that Saul plans to come to Keilah and destroy the city because of me.
MSG.11:
Will the city fathers of Keilah turn me over to him? Will Saul come down and do what I've heard? O God, God of Israel, tell me!"
God replied, "He's coming down."
MSG.12:
"And will the head men of Keilah turn me and my men over to Saul?"
And God said, "They'll turn you over."
MSG.13:
So David and his men got out of there. There were about six hundred of them. They left Keilah and kept moving, going here, there, wherever—always on the move.
When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he called off the raid.
MSG.14: David continued to live in desert hideouts and the backcountry wilderness hills of Ziph. Saul was out looking for him day after day, but God never turned David over to him.
MSG.15: David kept out of the way in the wilderness of Ziph, secluded at Horesh, since it was plain that Saul was determined to hunt him down.
MSG.16: Jonathan, Saul's son, visited David at Horesh and encouraged him in God.
MSG.17: He said, "Don't despair. My father, Saul, can't lay a hand on you. You will be Israel's king and I'll be right at your side to help. And my father knows it."
MSG.18: Then the two of them made a covenant before God. David stayed at Horesh and Jonathan went home.
MSG.19: Some Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Did you know that David is hiding out near us in the caves and canyons of Horesh? Right now he's at Hakilah Hill just south of Jeshimon.
MSG.20: So whenever you're ready to come down, we'd count it an honor to hand him over to the king."
MSG.21: Saul said, "God bless you for thinking about me!
MSG.22: Now go back and check everything out. Learn his routines. Observe his movements—where he goes, who he's with. He's very shrewd, you know.
MSG.23: Scout out all his hiding places. Then meet me at Nacon and I'll go with you. If he is anywhere to be found in all the thousands of Judah, I'll track him down!"
MSG.24:
So the Ziphites set out on their reconnaissance for Saul.
Meanwhile, David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the desert south of Jeshimon.
MSG.25: Saul and his men arrived and began their search. When David heard of it, he went south to Rock Mountain, camping out in the wilderness of Maon. Saul heard where he was and set off for the wilderness of Maon in pursuit.
MSG.26: Saul was on one side of the mountain, David and his men on the other. David was in full retreat, running, with Saul and his men closing in, about to get him.
MSG.27: Just then a messenger came to Saul and said, "Hurry! Come back! The Philistines have just attacked the country!"
MSG.28: So Saul called off his pursuit of David and went back to deal with the Philistines. That's how that place got the name Narrow Escape.
MSG.29: David left there and camped out in the caves and canyons of En Gedi.

NRSVCE.24: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of Jeshimon.
NRSVCE.25: Saul and his men went to search for him. When David was told, he went down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard that, he pursued David into the wilderness of Maon.
NRSVCE.26: Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain. David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were closing in on David and his men to capture them.
NRSVCE.27: Then a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and come; for the Philistines have made a raid on the land.”
NRSVCE.28: So Saul stopped pursuing David, and went against the Philistines; therefore that place was called the Rock of Escape.
NRSVCE.29: David then went up from there, and lived in the strongholds of En-gedi.

NET.1: They told David, “The Philistines are fighting in Keilah and are looting the threshing floors.”
NET.2: So David asked the LORD, “Should I go and strike down these Philistines?” The LORD said to David, “Go, strike down the Philistines and deliver Keilah.”
NET.3: But David’s men said to him, “We are afraid while we are still here in Judah! What will it be like if we go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?”
NET.4: So David asked the LORD once again. But again the LORD replied, “Arise, go down to Keilah, for I will give the Philistines into your hand.”
NET.5: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He took away their cattle and thoroughly defeated them. David delivered the inhabitants of Keilah.
NET.6: Now when Abiathar son of Ahimelech had fled to David at Keilah, he had brought with him an ephod.
NET.7: When Saul was told that David had come to Keilah, Saul said, “God has delivered him into my hand, for he has boxed himself into a corner by entering a city with two barred gates.”
NET.8: So Saul mustered all his army to go down to Keilah and besiege David and his men.
NET.9: When David realized that Saul was planning to harm him, he told Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod!”
NET.10: Then David said, “O LORD God of Israel, your servant has clearly heard that Saul is planning to come to Keilah to destroy the city because of me.
NET.11: Will the leaders of Keilah deliver me into his hand? Will Saul come down as your servant has heard? O LORD God of Israel, please inform your servant!” Then the LORD said, “He will come down.”
NET.12: David asked, “Will the leaders of Keilah deliver me and my men into Saul’s hand?” The LORD said, “They will deliver you over.”
NET.13: So David and his men, who numbered about six hundred, set out and left Keilah; they moved around from one place to another. When told that David had escaped from Keilah, Saul called a halt to his expedition.
NET.14: David stayed in the strongholds that were in the desert and in the hill country of the desert of Ziph. Saul looked for him all the time, but God did not deliver David into his hand.
NET.15: David realized that Saul had come out to seek his life; at that time David was in Horesh in the desert of Ziph.
NET.16: Then Jonathan son of Saul left and went to David at Horesh. He encouraged him through God.
NET.17: He said to him, “Don’t be afraid! For the hand of my father Saul cannot find you. You will rule over Israel, and I will be your second in command. Even my father Saul realizes this.”
NET.18: When the two of them had made a covenant before the LORD, David stayed on at Horesh, but Jonathan went to his house.
NET.19: Then the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Isn’t David hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh on the hill of Hakilah, south of Jeshimon?
NET.20: Now at your own discretion, O king, come down. Delivering him into the king’s hand will be our responsibility.”
NET.21: Saul replied, “May you be blessed by the LORD, for you have had compassion on me.
NET.22: Go and make further arrangements. Determine precisely where he is and who has seen him there, for I am told that he is extremely cunning.
NET.23: Locate precisely all the places where he hides and return to me with dependable information. Then I will go with you. If he is in the land, I will find him among all the thousands of Judah.”
NET.24: So they left and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the desert of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of Jeshimon.
NET.25: Saul and his men went to look for him. But David was informed and went down to the rock and stayed in the desert of Maon. When Saul heard about it, he pursued David in the desert of Maon.
NET.26: Saul went on one side of the mountain, while David and his men went on the other side of the mountain. David was hurrying to get away from Saul, but Saul and his men were surrounding David and his men so they could capture them.
NET.27: But a messenger came to Saul saying, “Come quickly, for the Philistines have raided the land!”
NET.28: So Saul stopped pursuing David and went to confront the Philistines. Therefore that place is called Sela Hammahlekoth.
NET.29: (24:1) Then David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En Gedi.
